eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model guidance for southern Ontario points to a cool, unsettled start to June with daytime highs near or slightly below seasonal norms around 20–23°C, driven by lingering high pressure and limited warm-air advection from the south. Traders have nonetheless priced a 66.5% chance of 28°C or higher on June 3, reflecting the high variability of early-summer temperature forecasts, the potential for faster-than-expected warming once any ridge builds, and the fact that even modest shifts in steering patterns or boundary-layer mixing can add several degrees within 48 hours. Shorter-range ensembles still show the bulk of probability mass below 25°C, which aligns with the 19% and 12% markets on 27°C and 26°C, while the thin tails below 24°C capture only low-probability cool outliers. The next 12–24 hours of updated runs from Environment and Climate Change Canada and the National Weather Service will be the key catalyst for any re-pricing ahead of resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current forecasts from multiple models place Chengdu’s June 3 maximum near 34–36 °C, aligning with the tight clustering of market-implied odds around those values. The Western Pacific subtropical high is expected to dominate, promoting subsidence and clear to partly cloudy skies that allow strong daytime solar heating, while the Sichuan Basin’s topography limits ventilation and amplifies the urban heat-island effect. Onset of the East Asian monsoon brings elevated humidity that can suppress peak temperatures through increased cloud cover or scattered showers, introducing the main source of forecast spread. China Meteorological Administration and global ensemble guidance show modest day-to-day revisions typical two days out, leaving traders focused on the next model cycle and any shifts in high-pressure positioning or moisture advection that could tip the outcome by one degree.
